title: Coherent coefficient comparisons for rational compact-support exchange
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A coefficient stage is a finite intermediate field of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
be a compact-support square with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its pulled-back compactification $c'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Assume the scheme and integral-operation hypotheses of [thm-cbc-finite-extension] at every coefficient stage: the four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional, $\ell$ is invertible on them, and $f$ is separated of finite type; $g$ is arbitrary. For each $W=X,Y,X',Y'$, work with the completed integral category $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{int}}_E(W)=\Dbc(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E(W)=\Dbc(W,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $(j_f,p_f)=(j,p)$ and $(j_{f'},p_{f'})=(j',p')$. For $h=f,f'$, put $H_{h,E}=Rh_{!,E}=Rp_{h,*,E}j_{h,!}$, the rational extensions [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] of the completed-coefficient compactification operations [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. For $u=g,g'$, write $P_{u,E}=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], extended to the raw rational categories. Write $T^W_{L/E}$, $a^W_{N,L,E}$ and $\sigma^W_{L/E}$ for the scalar extensions, associators and shift comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

For every inclusion $E\subseteq L$ of coefficient stages, there are specified exact natural isomorphisms
$$b^h_{L/E}:T^{\operatorname{target}(h)}_{L/E}H_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{h,L}T^{\operatorname{source}(h)}_{L/E}\qquad(h=f,f')$$
given by the proper direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] and the derived coefficient-change version of the localized ringed-site extension-by-zero tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. All equations below hold for every object $K$ in the source category of the displayed functors. They are comparisons between the stated raw PBC categories. They are identity for $L=E$, commute with the specified shifts, and for $E\subset L\subset N$ satisfy
$$b^h_{N/E,K}=H_{h,N}(a^X_{N,L,E,K})\,b^h_{N/L,T^X_{L/E}K}\,T^Y_{N/L}(b^h_{L/E,K})\,(a^Y_{N,L,E,H_{h,E}K})^{-1},$$
where in this equation $X=\operatorname{source}(h)$ and $Y=\operatorname{target}(h)$.

Let $d^u_{L/E}:T^{\operatorname{source}(u)}_{L/E}P_{u,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{u,L}T^{\operatorname{target}(u)}_{L/E}$ be the pullback comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and set $U_E=P_{g,E}H_{f,E}$ and $V_E=H_{f',E}P_{g',E}$. Their composite coefficient comparisons are
$$b^U_{L/E,K}=P_{g,L}(b^f_{L/E,K})\,d^g_{L/E,H_{f,E}K},\qquad
b^V_{L/E,K}=H_{f',L}(d^{g'}_{L/E,K})\,b^{f'}_{L/E,P_{g',E}K}.$$
Let $\eta_E:U_E\Rightarrow V_E$ be the rationalization of the specified completed compact-support exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], without any change of its strict-tower normalization. These comparisons intertwine that actual exchange:
$$\eta_{L,T^X_{L/E}K}\,b^U_{L/E,K}=b^V_{L/E,K}\,T^{Y'}_{L/E}(\eta_{E,K}).$$
This statement asserts coefficient coherence, not invertibility of $\eta_E$, and uses neither smoothness nor a base-field hypothesis.

proof.text: Work first with integral ambient derived categories, writing $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$, and $C_W=(-)\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S_W$ is finite free over $R_W$, $C_W$ preserves complete objects, and its specified quotient-tower comparison $\chi$ is the natural isomorphism with the actual integral coefficient extension. Choose an $R_W$-module basis of $S_W$ only for checking isomorphisms at a fixed scheme: it identifies the underlying $R_W$-module functor $C_W$ with a finite biproduct of copies of the identity. Tensor with $S_W$ is therefore exact. All maps below are the canonical balanced maps, independent of this checking basis. The coefficient identifications for scheme inverse image, open restriction and quotient maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]; its naturality in the inverse system identifies the two coefficient maps in every square. Work at intermediate compactification schemes in ambient categories: no constructibility assertion for an intermediate factor is being assumed.

proof.text: For $k:U\hookrightarrow W$ equal to $j$ or $j'$, construct $\lambda_k:C_Wk_{!,R}\longrightarrow k_{!,S}C_U$. On the direct-sum extension presheaf its formula is $(i_\alpha x)\otimes s\mapsto i_\alpha(x\otimes s)$, where $i_\alpha$ denotes a summand indexed by a map to the open. The inverse of the natural tensor isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], with $\mathcal F=S_W$, is exactly this map after sheafification. It is $S_W$-linear: multiplying $s$ by $s'$ on either side gives $i_\alpha(x\otimes ss')$; balancing over $R_W$ gives the same formula. Thus it is an isomorphism of $S_W$-module sheaves, not merely of underlying $R_W$-modules. Extension by zero is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and tensor with $S_W$ is exact by step 1. Applying the isomorphism degreewise computes both derived functors; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] supplies the exact derived functors and their shift comparisons. This proves the required derived coefficient-change version without treating the underived tensor lemma itself as a derived or completed assertion.

proof.text: Check the coherence of $\lambda$ on the same summands. For $E\subset L\subset N$ the successive-extension composite sends $((i_\alpha x)\otimes s)\otimes z$ to $i_\alpha(x\otimes sz)$ after the balanced associators; the one-step comparison sends it to precisely that element. These maps respect restrictions and therefore descend to sheafification and complexes. For the repeated field, the tensor unit sends $(i_\alpha x)\otimes1$ to $i_\alpha x$; after the literal identity normalization of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] this is the identity. The maps have degree zero and are degreewise, so commuting them with a cochain shift introduces no sign; their shift square is the one supplied in step 2. This establishes the open-factor unit, successive-field and shift equations, with the specified balanced associators.

proof.text: For any scheme map $q:Z\to W$ used below, let $\pi_q:C_WRq_{*,R}\to Rq_{*,S}C_Z$ be the projection comparison: its adjunct is the counit tensored with $1_{S_Z}$, with the canonical pullback/tensor balancing. The coefficient identifications of step 1 identify $Lq^*S_W$ with $S_Z$. Its adic hypotheses hold for $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(t)$: $A$ is a Noetherian domain because it is a DVR [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], its quotients are finite [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$ is a two-term finite-free resolution of $A/t^n$, since $t^n\neq0$. The finite-free clause of [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], applied to the finite free $R_W$-module $S_W$, therefore makes $\pi_q$ invertible. Its map is $S_W$-linear by its counit-tensor formula. The derived comparison really has the displayed $S$-coefficient target: restriction of scalars preserves K-injectives, since its left adjoint $C$ is exact and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies. Thus the same direct-image complexes compute its underlying $R$-module map. The tensor-unit case of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] fixes the unit normalization. Its stated shift square is in the tensor variable; check the shift in the input $M$ as follows. Choose a basis of $S_W$ and pull it back to a basis of $S_Z$. On underlying $R$-modules the comparison is then $\bigoplus_{i=1}^{[L:E]}Rq_*M\to Rq_*(\bigoplus_i M)$. The adjunct on each summand is the counit, so the adjunction triangle identity identifies each summand map with $1_{Rq_*M}$. Finite biproducts and termwise direct image commute with cochain shift, and a shifted K-injective representative remains K-injective (maps from an acyclic $A$ into $I[1]$ are maps from the acyclic $A[-1]$ into $I$). Thus this finite-biproduct map has the canonical input-shift square. The coefficient identifications of step 1 make module pullback exact, so the derived counit on a K-injective $I$ is represented by the termwise ordinary counit $q^*q_*I\to I$. Replacing $I$ by $I[1]$ represents its shift by the preceding K-injectivity check. For equality as $S$-module derived maps, transpose the input-shift square under the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction: on complexes its two adjuncts are the shifted counit tensored with the degree-zero scalar factor. The scalar factor has degree zero, so the tensor shift identification contributes no sign, and the adjuncts agree. The adjunction bijection proves the asserted $S$-linear input-shift square. For successive coefficient fields, transpose the two candidate composites under the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction: both give $(\varepsilon\otimes1\otimes1)$ followed by multiplication of the two scalar factors, on $Lq^*Rq_*M\otimes S\otimes S'$. Adjunction is a bijection on these Hom sets, so the composites agree. This proves the successive-field equation for $\pi$, with the balanced associators, on ambient categories for $p,p'$ as well. It is the proper direct-image comparison specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

proof.text: Record carefully how scalar extension interacts with completion units. Let $\Lambda_R,\Lambda_{S,t},\Lambda_{S,v}$ denote the Koszul completion reflectors. The DVR description in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives $t=u v^e$ in $\mathcal O_L$, with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$ (the restricted absolute value gives $0<|t|_L<1$). The local completeness conditions for $(t)$ and $(v)$ in $S_W$ agree: an element of $(t)$ lies in $(v)$, and for any local $a\in(v)$ one has $a^e\in(t)$ and $S_W[1/a]=S_W[1/a^e]$. Hence the Hom-bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] gives a unique unit-preserving natural isomorphism $\Lambda_{S,t}\cong\Lambda_{S,v}$. Tensor with the finite free $S_W$ commutes with the strict Koszul-tower limit: after the basis check in step 1, the comparison with products is the finite-biproduct rearrangement $\bigoplus_{i=1}^d\prod_n^D X_n\cong\prod_n^D\bigoplus_{i=1}^d X_n$; it commutes with $1-s$ and hence with the natural Roos limit triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. At index $n$, tensor sends $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ to $[S_W\xrightarrow{t^n}S_W]$ and sends the transition $(t,1)$ to $(t,1)$. It therefore gives a unit-preserving isomorphism $C_W\Lambda_R\cong\Lambda_{S,t}C_W\cong\Lambda_{S,v}C_W$. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] the quotient-tower units are these same units. In particular these are comparisons for the actual completed functors, including the specified $\chi$ in step 1, not arbitrary identifications of complete endpoints.

proof.text: Check the completed open-square comparison $\beta$ with these scalar maps. A flat-term K-flat representative exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Extension by zero preserves it: for any acyclic complex $A$ on the larger site, $(j_!P)\otimes A=j_!(P\otimes j^*A)$ by the summand tensor formula, the inner complex is acyclic by K-flatness and exact restriction, and exact $j_!$ preserves acyclicity; the same argument for degree-zero modules proves flatness of its terms. Here $j_!$ commutes with the direct sums in total tensor because it is a left adjoint: maps from $j_!(\bigoplus P_i)$ to $B$ are the families of maps $P_i\to j^*B$, which are the maps from $\bigoplus j_!P_i$ to $B$. Thus the tensor formula also computes $j_!$ against derived finite reduction, not merely underived reduction. The derived-tensor descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes these representative calculations independent of the resolution. For each $n$, use coefficients $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_W$ and $S_n=(\mathcal O_L/t^n)_W$, a finite free extension of finite ring sheaves: [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies these sheaves with $R_W/t^nR_W$ and $S_W/t^nS_W$ (for the latter use $(t^n)=(v^{en})$); reduce the finite-free isomorphism of step 1 modulo $t^n$. The finite-coefficient open base-change map of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] is the map on extension summands induced by pullback to the open; its coefficient square with $\lambda$ commutes, since either order takes $(i_\alpha x)\otimes s$ to $i_{\alpha'}(g'^*x\otimes s)$. This description also follows by transposing under the exact localized-site adjunction of step 2: both adjoints restrict to $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes s$ on the open. The equality is natural in the ring quotient, so is an equality of maps of strict diagram complexes, not just of individual derived evaluations. Use the diagram-site realization [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] to form these derived tensor and pullback comparisons on one small site. Taking the derived limit and using the unit-preserving comparison of step 5 gives the coefficient square for completed pullbacks and $\beta$, as defined in [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. To check the $L$-tower normalization explicitly, $(t^n)=(v^{en})$; the $t$-tower is the indicated subsequence of the $v$-tower, with the same quotient maps. Its derived-limit restriction is a unit-preserving isomorphism: in the Roos complex of step 5 eliminate each finite block between retained indices by $x_i=y_i+s_i x_{i+1}$. The remaining equation at a retained index $en$ is $x_{en}-s_{en,e(n+1)}x_{e(n+1)}=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}s_{en,i}y_i$; the other equations give contractible identity factors, including the finite initial block. Thus the resulting limit comparison is the same unit-preserving comparison of step 5. The comparison between $j_!$ and the reduction-tower limit in the definition of $\beta$ commutes with these restriction maps: both are induced by the same quotient-cone components, and the displayed strict square commutes with them. Consequently this argument applies to the specified $v$-normalized $\beta_L$, not a replacement map. In notation $P_u=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and $d_u:C P_{u,R}\cong P_{u,S}C$, the equality just proved is $(j'_!d_{g'})\lambda_{j',P_{g',R}K}C(\beta_R)=\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_{j,K})d_{\bar g',j_!K}$. The $d$ here is the canonical completed balancing comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], since the construction preserves the ordinary tensor balancing and its completion unit.

proof.text:
For the proper square $(p,p',g,\bar g')$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] with coefficient object $S_Y$. The hypotheses are ringed-topos commutation and the canonical derived adjunctions; the square has those coefficient maps by step 1. Its two composites say that the ambient mate $e_M$ commutes with the scalar projection maps $\pi_p,\pi_{p'}$ and ordinary pullback/tensor balancing. The comparison with the $S$-coefficient mate uses the same counits; restriction of scalars computes their derived direct images as in step 4. Pass to completed pullbacks using step 5. To see equality of the resulting arrows, precompose with the $S$-completion unit of $C_{Y'}Lg_R^*Rp_{*,R}M$. The characterization in step 7 reduces both composites to that ambient tensor-mate equation, followed by $Rp'_* $ of the completion unit on the target. The target is complete, so the reflector Hom-bijection makes the two completed arrows equal. Hence, writing $\pi$ and $d$ at their appropriate schemes, one has
$\gamma_{S,C M}\,P_{g,S}(\pi_{p,M})\,d_{g,Rp_*M}=Rp'_{*,S}(d_{\bar g',M})\,\pi_{p',P_{\bar g',R}M}\,C_{Y'}(\gamma_{R,M})$.
All identifications here are the specified ones: step 7 fixed $H,H',v_\bullet$ and step 5 fixed the units. This establishes coefficient compatibility for the actual proper factor, not merely for an unspecified completed mate.

proof.text: Define the integral compact-support comparison by the ordered composite $b^h=Rp_{h,*,S}(\lambda_{j_h})\,\pi_{p_h,j_{h,!}(-)}$. The definition $H_h=Rp_{h,*}j_{h,!}$ is [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Steps 2 and 4 make this an exact natural isomorphism. Its source and target on the final schemes lie in the indicated integral constructible categories: use [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] for $H_h$ and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] for $C$; the completed pullback restrictions are proved as follows. Let $u:T'\to T$ be $g$ or $g'$ (the schemes $T,T'$ are among the four noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with $\ell$ invertible) and let $M\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{int}}_E(T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] (iii), $M$ is bounded, say with cohomology in $[a,b]$. The two-term finite free resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{t^n}\mathcal O_E]$ of $\mathcal O_E/t^n$ [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect], tensored with the flat completed coefficient sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], computes the reduction $M_n$ as the cone of $t^n:M\to M$, so every reduction has cohomology in $[a-1,b]$, independently of $n$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] to the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with vertical maps $\mathrm{id}_T,\mathrm{id}_{T'}$ and both horizontal maps $u$: the identities are proper with geometric fibres of dimension at most $e=0$, and $N=\ell$ annihilates the residue field $\mathcal O_E/t$ and is invertible on $T,T'$. Its conclusion $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\in\Dbc$ for this square gives $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{int}}_E(T')$. On the inherited triangulations of [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], the restricted completed pullback is exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear: by [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] it is reduction tower, derived tower pullback and derived limit, each exact (the limit by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]) and each carrying $rv$ to $r$ times the image of $v$. This is the hypothesis on $P_{u}$ used by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] in step 11. The base-change statement [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] supplies separated finite type for $f'$. The same argument applies to the pulled-back compactification, since it is a compactification of $f'$ by [def-cbc-compact-support-square]; the quasi-compactness of the opens is stated in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. There is no need to restrict $j_!$ and $Rp_*$ separately to a constructible category on $\overline X$. The unit law follows by composing the unit laws in steps 3 and 4, and the shift square is the composite of their shift squares. For a tower of fields, substitute the two successive-field equations of those steps in $Rp_*(\lambda)\pi$; naturality of $\pi$ moves the inner $\lambda$ past $\pi$, and the middle inverse associators cancel. The remaining factors, in order, are $H_{h,N}(a^{\mathrm{source}(h)})$, $b^h_{N/L,C_{L/E}K}$, $C_{N/L}(b^h_{L/E,K})$, and $(a^{\mathrm{target}(h)})^{-1}$. This is exactly the displayed $b^h$ equation of the item.

proof.text: Prove the integral compact-support exchange equation by pasting the two established squares. Set $M=j_!K$ and $B=Rp'_*(\beta)\gamma_M$, exactly the ordered composite in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Start with $B_{S,CK}P_{g,S}(b^f)d_{g,H_fK}$. Replace $b^f$ by $Rp_{*,S}(\lambda_j)\pi_p$. Naturality of $\gamma_S$ with respect to $\lambda_j$ changes the initial portion to $Rp'_{*,S}(\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_j))\gamma_{S,CM}P_{g,S}(\pi_p)d_g$. Replace the latter three factors using the proper equality of step 8. Inside $Rp'_{*,S}$ the consecutive factors are then $\beta_{S,CK}P_{\bar g',S}(\lambda_j)d_{\bar g',j_!K}$; step 6 replaces them by $(j'_!d_{g'})\lambda_{j',P_{g',R}K}C(\beta_R)$. Naturality of $\pi_{p'}$ moves $C(\beta_R)$ to the right across that projection comparison. The remaining left factors are $H_{f',S}(d_{g'})b^{f'}_{P_{g',R}K}$, and the right factors are $C(Rp'_*(\beta_R)\gamma_{R,j_!K})=C(B_{R,K})$. Therefore $B_{S,CK}b^U=b^V C(B_{R,K})$, with $b^U=P_{g,S}(b^f)d^g$ and $b^V=H_{f',S}(d^{g'})b^{f'}$. This calculation uses no invertibility of $B$ or $\gamma$.

source.place: Opening exchange paragraph; explicit pasting of the proper and open coefficient squares

proof.text: Finally localize the integral functors and comparisons. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] there are no new objects: a rational arrow is a finite sum of $u\otimes a$, with integral $u$ and $a\in E$. By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], the exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear $H,P$ and all their integral natural transformations extend, with component $\eta_K\otimes1$. For the scalar functor the extension on such an arrow is $C(u)\otimes\iota_{L/E}(a)$; this is well defined by balancing, since $C(ru)=\iota(r)C(u)$ and every nonzero $r\in\mathcal O_E$ becomes invertible in $L$. Thus an integral naturality square multiplied by $\iota(a)$ is the required rational naturality square for $u\otimes a$, and additivity handles a general arrow. Apply localization to the equations of steps 3, 4, 9 and 10: it preserves compositions, identities, inverses and shifts. The scalar associators and shifts are those of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], whose integral comparisons were used above. Consequently the rational $b^h$ have the displayed unit, shift and successive-extension laws, their composite comparisons are the stated $b^U,b^V$, and step 10 becomes $\eta_{L,TK}b^U=b^V T(\eta_{E,K})$ for the rationalization of precisely the specified strict-normalized exchange. All hypotheses used were the stated integral-operation domains, finite coefficient extensions and the compactification geometry; no base-field or smoothness assumption was introduced.

split_report.summary: Preserved the full statement and split the missing coefficient coherence into explicit open-module tensor, counit projection, completion-unit, strict-normalization, pasting and rationalization arguments. Reused existing generic tools and same-unit completed-open lemmas. Corrected the draft misuse of an underived tensor identity and of ordinary-exchange coherence as if they directly stated completed compact-support coherence. No new nodes. Second reader made the adic hypotheses, input-variable shift check, and commutation with total-tensor sums explicit. Maintainer reader added to step 9 the explicit restriction of completed pullback to the integral PBC categories (prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible with the identity-vertical square), which step 11 needs for rational transport.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N3-34d3a34e1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the full statement of each of its 30 dependencies (all exist, none merged), all of def-cbc-completed-exchange-map, and the proof of prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension. The proof's π (projection mate with coefficient object S_Y) and d (ordinary balancing completed with the unit-fixed reflector isomorphism) are the comparisons that proposition specifies. Source checked: blueprint main-20261015 thm-cbc-qbar.proof.md, opening paragraph. Its j_! citation, lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula, is stated for a finite ring Λ and does not apply to O_E. The item's use of the ringed-slice tensor lemma, with finite-Λ open base change only at finite levels, is therefore a justified replacement. The item's statement is unchanged, it has no new nodes, and it cites no SGA source. Steps checked: 4 (the projection-formula hypotheses hold: O_E is a DVR, its quotients are finite and perfect, and S_W is finite free); 5 (t=uv^e with e≥1, so the (t)- and (v)-completeness conditions agree); 6 (the en-subsequence Roos elimination is correct; the final equation has the right type); 7 (sν=Rlim(H)ρ_N and cν'=Rlim(H')ρ_F, so γν=ν'e, and the extension is unique by the reflector); 8 (precomposing with C(ν) reduces it to the ambient tensor/exchange coherence); 10 (I redid the pasting by hand: B_S b^U = b^V C(B_R)); 11 (the localization extension is well defined). Edge cases checked: K=0, empty open, identity open, L=E, e=1 and e>1, n=1. Not duplicates: lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence and def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport. One fault, C1/C3, fixed: step 9 claimed without a citation that completed pullback restricts to the integral PBC categories. Step 11 needs that so P_g and P_g' are exact O_E-linear for prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport, and it is proved only inside thm-cbc-finite-extension's proof. The corrected node file is in fixes/. It spells out the argument: lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization(iii) and lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect give a uniform reduction interval; prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible is applied to the identity-vertical cartesian square (e=0, N=ℓ); exactness comes from def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit and lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated. proof_deps were recomputed (35 nodes). The four new off-unit tools were added to tool_uses with reasons. I accept all 25 tool_uses.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
